Component: Freenove Control Board.

Purpose: Demonstrates the layout and port locations of the black Freenove control board.

Technical details:
- Top headers (DIGITAL/PWM): SCL, SDA, AREF, GND, 13, 12, ~11, ~10, ~9, 8, 7, ~6, ~5, 4, ~3, 2, TX->1, RX<-0.
- Left side: Reset button, USB interface, DC interface.
- Center LEDs: L, TX, RX, ON.
- Right side: ICSP header (6 pins).
- Bottom headers:
    - POWER: IOREF, RESET, 3.3V, 5V, GND, GND, Vin.
    - ANALOG IN: A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Freenove Control Board (Blue).

Purpose: Illustrates the layout, ports, and indicators of the Freenove control board used for circuit programming and component control.

Technical details:
- Top headers: AREF, GND, and Digital/PWM pins labeled 13, 12, 11 (~), 10 (~), 9 (~), 8, 7, 6 (~), 5 (~), 4, 3 (~), 2, TX (1), RX (0).
- Indicators: LED L, LED TX, LED RX, and LED ON.
- Bottom headers: Power pins (IOREF, RESET, 3.3V, 5V, GND, GND, Vin) and Analog Input pins (A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5).
- Interfaces: USB (left side), DC power jack (bottom left), ICSP header (top left), and ICSP header (right side).
- Components: RESET button (top left).
- Branding: "FREENOVE" logo and "FREENOVE.COM" printed on the board.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Freenove Control Board (Black).
Purpose: Illustrates the layout, pin headers, and interface locations of the control board.
Technical details: 
- Digital/PWM section includes pins labeled: SCL, SDA, AREF, GND, 13, 12, ~11, ~10, ~9, 8, 7, ~6, ~5, 4, ~3, 2, TX->1, RX<-0.
- Power section pins: IOREF, RESET, 3.3V, 5V, GND, Vin.
- Analog IN section pins: A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5.
- On-board LEDs labeled: L, TX, RX, ON.
- Physical interfaces: USB (left side), DC barrel jack (bottom left), and 6-pin ICSP header (middle right).
- Features a physical "RESET" button at the top left.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Arduino software download interface.
Purpose: Demonstrates the download page for Arduino IDE version 2.3.6.
Technical details: The image shows a screenshot of the Arduino IDE interface (configured for Arduino Uno) and a web interface for software installation. The web interface displays:
- Software Title: "Arduino IDE 2.3.6"
- Installer selector dropdown: "Windows Win 10 or newer (64-bit)"
- Action button: "DOWNLOAD"
- Secondary section: "Nightly Builds" with a description for downloading preview releases.
- Footer text: "The Arduino IDE 2.0 is open source and its source code is hosted on GitHub."
The IDE screenshot illustrates the code editor window with "weatherstation.ino" file open, showing standard `void setup()` and `void loop()` structures.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Arduino Software (IDE) download interface.

Purpose: Demonstrates the download selection menu for various Arduino IDE versions and operating systems.

Technical details:
- Version featured: Arduino IDE 2.3.6.
- Download dropdown menu options: "Windows Win 10 or newer (64-bit)", "Windows MSI installer", "Windows ZIP file", "Linux AppImage (64-bit X86-64)", "Linux ZIP file (64-bit X86-64)", "macOS Intel 10.15 Catalina or newer (64-bit)", and "macOS Apple Silicon 11 Big Sur or newer (64-bit)".
- The image displays screenshots of the Arduino IDE 2 editor window showing `void setup()` and `void loop()` functions.
- A secondary section labeled "Legacy IDE (1.8.19)" is visible at the bottom for downloading older software versions.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Arduino IDE 2.3.6 interface window.

Purpose: Demonstrates the layout of the Arduino Integrated Development Environment, including code editing and device connection status.

Technical details:
- Top Menu: File, Edit, Sketch, Tools, Help.
- Toolbar (left to right): Verify button, Upload button, Debug button, "Arduino Uno" board selection dropdown, Serial Plotter button, Serial Monitor button.
- Text Editor: Displays a default "sketch_sep17a.ino" file containing `setup()` and `loop()` functions with lines 1-10 numbered.
- Console/Output: Displays the "Output" area at the bottom.
- Status Bar: Bottom right indicates "Ln 10, Col 1" and "Arduino Uno on COM30" (configured board and serial port).
- Navigation Sidebar: Icons for Folder, Sketchbook, Library Manager, Board Manager, Search, and Account.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit Knowledge graphics.
Purpose: Demonstrates the waveform characteristics of Direct Current (DC) and Alternating Current (AC).
Technical details: The image contains two Cartesian graphs plotting Voltage/Current (U/I) on the vertical axis against time (t) on the horizontal axis. 
- The left graph titled "Direct Current" features a horizontal blue line representing a constant U/I value over time.
- The right graph titled "Alternating Current" features a green sinusoidal wave representing periodic fluctuation of U/I over time.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit schematic symbol.
Purpose: This image depicts the standardized electronic symbol for a battery or battery pack.
Technical details: The symbol consists of two parallel vertical lines of unequal length representing the battery plates, flanked by a positive (+) sign on the left and a negative (-) sign on the right. Red horizontal lines labeled "2" and "1" extend from the plates toward the left and right poles, respectively.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit symbol for a battery or battery pack.

Purpose: This image depicts the schematic representation of a battery power source, demonstrating the standard symbol format.

Technical details: The symbol consists of two pairs of parallel vertical lines of alternating length (long and short) representing battery cells. A "+" sign is positioned to the left of the symbol, and a "-" sign is positioned to the right. Red highlights over the lines indicate connection points labeled "2" on the left and "1" on the right.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Battery illustration.
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical representation of an AA battery used in the "Circuit Knowledge" section.
Technical details: The image shows a cylindrical battery with a positive terminal (+) at the top and a negative terminal (-) at the bottom. Text labeled "AA Battery" is oriented vertically along the body of the cell.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit Knowledge section.
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical appearance of two "AA Battery" units connected in series.
Technical details: The image shows two identical batteries positioned horizontally, connected positive-to-negative. Each battery is labeled "AA Battery" with a vertical "-" symbol on the left (negative end) and a "+" symbol on the right (positive end).

Component: Circuit diagram component illustration.
Purpose: Demonstrates a series configuration of two AA batteries.
Technical details: The image shows two "AA Battery" units stacked vertically. The top battery has its positive (+) terminal at the top and negative (-) terminal at the bottom. The bottom battery is stacked such that its positive (+) terminal is in contact with the negative terminal of the top battery, and its negative (-) terminal is at the bottom.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Schematic diagrams.
Purpose: Demonstrates closed-loop versus open-loop circuit conditions.
Technical details: Both diagrams contain a 5V power supply symbol at the top, a resistor labeled R1, and a ground symbol at the bottom. The resistor has pins labeled "2" at the top and "1" at the bottom.
Left diagram: Shows a complete circuit where the 5V source connects to R1 pin 2, and R1 pin 1 connects to the ground symbol via a continuous vertical line.
Right diagram: Shows an open circuit where the connection is broken between R1 pin 1 and the ground symbol; the segment extending downward from R1 pin 1 is colored red, while the segment extending upward from the ground symbol is green, indicating a lack of continuity.

Component: Resistor illustration.
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical appearance of a resistor alongside its corresponding circuit schematic symbol.
Technical details: The image shows a physical resistor on the left with two leads labeled "1" at the top and "2" at the bottom. To the right is the standard zigzag schematic symbol for a resistor, also labeled with "1" at the top terminal and "2" at the bottom terminal.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Electrical schematic diagram.
Purpose: Demonstrates a basic DC voltage divider or pull-down configuration connected to ground.
Technical details: The circuit consists of a 5V power source connected in series with a resistor (R1) rated at 10kΩ, which then connects to ground (GND). The resistor has two terminal labels, "2" at the top end and "1" at the bottom end.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Breadboard internal connection diagram.

Purpose: Demonstrates the electrical connectivity of the holes within a standard breadboard.

Technical details: 
- The image displays columns 1 through 30.
- Rows A, B, C, D, and E are linked vertically in green segments for each column.
- Rows F, G, H, I, and J are linked vertically in green segments for each column.
- The top two power rails are connected horizontally: the top rail (indicated by a blue line) is a single continuous row, and the rail below it (indicated by a red line) is a single continuous row.
- The bottom two power rails are connected horizontally: the rail above the red line (indicated by a blue line) is a single continuous row, and the bottom rail (indicated by a red line) is a single continuous row.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Push Button Switch.

Purpose: Demonstrates the physical pin layout and the internal electrical schematic of a 4-pin momentary push button switch.

Technical details: 
- The image displays a top-down view of a 4-pin switch on the left and its corresponding schematic symbol on the right. 
- The pins are labeled "1" and "2" at each corner. 
- In the schematic, the two pins on the left (labeled 1) are internally connected, and the two pins on the right (labeled 2) are internally connected. 
- The diagonal bridge in the schematic symbol indicates the momentary contact point between the left side (1) and the right side (2) when the button is pressed. 
- Nearby text confirms that the left two pins are connected, and the right two pins are connected, with the circuit completing when the button is pressed.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: LED (Light Emitting Diode)
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical appearance and circuit schematic symbol of an LED, highlighting its polar nature.
Technical details: The left side shows a physical LED with two leads labeled "1" (the longer lead with a "+" sign) and "2" (the shorter lead with a "-" sign). The right side shows the corresponding circuit symbol, where terminal "1" corresponds to the anode (+) and terminal "2" corresponds to the cathode (-). Arrows pointing away from the diode symbol indicate light emission.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Schematic diagram for Project 1.1 Control LED with Manual Button.

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit path for controlling an LED with a push button switch using a 5V power supply.

Technical details: The circuit is a series loop starting from a 5V power source connected to terminal 2 of resistor R1 (220Ω). Terminal 1 of R1 connects to terminal 2 of push button switch S1. Terminal 1 of S1 connects to the anode (terminal 1) of LED1. The cathode (terminal 2) of LED1 connects to ground. The schematic depicts the components in a single vertical path.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Breadboard, push button switch, LED, resistor, and Freenove control board.
Purpose: Demonstrates the hardware wiring for controlling an LED with a manual push button switch.
Technical details: The breadboard hosts a push button switch at coordinates (C, 16) through (E, 18). An LED is inserted with its cathode in column 14 (row E) and its anode in column 14 (row F). A resistor connects row E, column 17 to row E, column 21. A black jumper wire connects the breadboard row E, column 14 to the control board GND pin. A red jumper wire connects the breadboard row E, column 21 to the control board 5V pin (implied power). The control board features pins labeled SCL, SDA, AREF, GND, 13, 12, ~11, ~10, ~9, 8, ~5, 4, ~3, 2, TX->1, RX<-0.
Uncertainty: The exact resistance value of the component is unreadable from the visual representation. The power connection from the breadboard to the control board 5V pin is partially obscured by the edge of the image frame.

Component: Circuit Knowledge charts.
Purpose: Demonstrates the visual difference between analog and digital signals.
Technical details:
- Two graphs are presented with "U" (voltage) on the vertical axis and "t" (time) on the horizontal axis.
- Left graph labeled "ANALOG" shows a continuous, smooth, variable green wave.
- Right graph labeled "DIGITAL" shows a discrete, square-wave blue signal that switches between two distinct levels.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit Knowledge graph.

Purpose: Demonstrates the representation of digital signals using high (5V) and low (0V) voltage levels over time, corresponding to binary 1 and 0.

Technical details: The graph plots voltage (U) on the vertical axis against time (t) on the horizontal axis. A square wave oscillates between 0V and 5V. The segments at 5V are labeled "1", and the segments at 0V are labeled "0". The sequence depicted is 1, 0, 1, 0, 1.

Component: Breadboard and Freenove control board.
Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit connection to blink an LED using the control board's digital pin 13.
Technical details:
- LED: Anode connected to control board pin 13 via a yellow jumper wire; cathode connected to ground (GND) on the control board via a black jumper wire and a resistor.
- Resistor: Placed on the breadboard, bridging the LED cathode column and the column connected to the GND pin.
- Control Board Pin Headers: Connections are made to "13" and "GND" in the digital pin header block. 
- Breadboard: Features standard numbered rows (5 to 30 visible).
Uncertainty: Resistor color bands are visible but the resistance value is not explicitly labeled in the text or diagram.

Component: Circuit schematic for LED control.
Purpose: Demonstrates the connection between a control board digital pin and an LED.
Technical details: The circuit shows a series connection starting from "Pin 13" (top), connected to terminal 2 of resistor "R1" (value 220Ω), which connects at terminal 1 to the anode (terminal 1) of "LED1". The cathode (terminal 2) of "LED1" connects to a ground symbol at the bottom. Green lines indicate the conductive path.

Component: Breadboard connection view.
Purpose: Demonstrates the insertion of a standard through-hole red LED into a breadboard.
Technical details: The LED is inserted into the breadboard with its leads spanning two adjacent terminal rows. The numerical label "15" is visible at the top edge, indicating the row alignment for the LED's cathode/anode pins. The LED is oriented such that its cathode (shorter lead) and anode (longer lead) are positioned in separate breadboard contact holes.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Breadboard and Freenove Control Board.
Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit connection for the "Two LEDs Blink" project.
Technical details: Two red LEDs are inserted into the breadboard at row H, column 20 and column 22. Each LED anode is connected to a resistor in the same column (row D). Resistor terminals at row C, column 20 and column 22 are connected to the control board digital pins 5 and 4, respectively, via yellow and green wires. Both LED cathodes (row H, column 20 and column 22) are connected to the common ground rail (negative rail) of the breadboard. A black wire connects the breadboard's ground rail to the GND pin on the control board.
Uncertainty: Wire colors and exact pin-to-row alignment are based on visual observation of the diagram.

Component: Circuit schematic for Project 2.1 Two LEDs Blink.

Purpose: Demonstrates the connection of two LEDs to a microcontroller interface.

Technical details:
- Two identical branches are shown, each consisting of a pin input, an LED, and a 220Ω resistor connected to ground.
- Left branch: "Pin 4" connects to the anode (pin 1) of LED1. The cathode (pin 2) of LED1 connects to pin 2 of resistor R1 (220Ω). Pin 1 of R1 connects to ground.
- Right branch: "Pin 5" connects to the anode (pin 1) of LED2. The cathode (pin 2) of LED2 connects to pin 2 of resistor R2 (220Ω). Pin 1 of R2 connects to ground.
- All LED and resistor pins are labeled 1 and 2.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Breadboard interface.
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical mounting of two LEDs in a breadboard for Project 2.1.
Technical details: The image shows two identical red LEDs inserted into a breadboard with vertical column spacing. Each LED has two leads inserted into separate, adjacent contacts. The breadboard features standard socket holes. No electrical component labels, pin identifiers, or schematic connection points are visible on the breadboard itself.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: LED bar graph.
Purpose: Displays the pinout configuration for an LED bar graph component.
Technical details: The image shows a 10-segment LED bar graph labeled "KYX-B10R" on the left side. It features two parallel rows of 10 pins each, totaling 20 pins. The pins are numbered 1 through 10 along the left edge (top-to-bottom) and 20 through 11 along the right edge (top-to-bottom). Pin 1 is opposite pin 20, pin 2 is opposite pin 19, and so on, down to pin 10 opposite pin 11.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: LED bar graph schematic diagram.

Purpose: This image illustrates the internal pin configuration of a 10-segment LED bar graph.

Technical details: The diagram displays 10 individual LED symbols arranged vertically, representing a 10-LED integration. Each LED has two connection points represented by pins numbered 1 through 20.
- Pin 1 corresponds to the input for the first LED, with pin 20 serving as the corresponding opposite pole.
- The pins are arranged sequentially: 2 matches with 19, 3 with 18, 4 with 17, 5 with 16, 6 with 15, 7 with 14, 8 with 13, 9 with 12, and 10 with 11.
- Each horizontal line connects a numbered pin to the anode/cathode of an individual LED symbol.

Uncertainty: The diagram does not explicitly label which side of the LED symbol (left or right) corresponds to the positive or negative pole; users should refer to the text regarding potential reverse connection troubleshooting.

Component: Breadboard and Freenove Control Board.
Purpose: Demonstrates the hardware wiring for an LED bar graph display project.
Technical details: 
- An LED bar graph is inserted into the breadboard, with eight individual resistors connecting its anode pins to the power bus.
- Control board pins are connected to the breadboard rows as follows: 
  - GND pin to the negative power rail.
  - Pin 12 to the first LED anode row (via yellow wire).
  - Pin 11 to the second LED anode row (via green wire).
  - Pin 10 to the third LED anode row (via grey wire).
  - Pin 9 to the fourth LED anode row (via white wire).
  - Pin 8 to the fifth LED anode row (via orange wire).
  - Pin 7 to the sixth LED anode row (via brown wire).
  - Pin 6 to the seventh LED anode row (via light blue wire).
  - Pin 5 to the eighth LED anode row (via dark brown wire).
  - Pin 4 to the ninth LED anode row (via magenta wire).
Uncertainty: The tenth LED position is not connected to a control pin. Wire colors are subject to visual interpretation.

Component: Schematic diagram for an LED Bar Graph project.

Purpose: Demonstrates the hardware connection between a control board and an LED bar graph.

Technical details:
- Control board pins D12, D11, D10, D9, D8, D7, D6, D5, D4, and D3 are connected to the anodes of ten LEDs (labeled 1 through 10 at the cathodes).
- Each LED (1–10) corresponds to an opposite pin (20–11) connected through 220Ω resistors (R1–R10).
- All resistors (R1–R10) are tied to a common ground connection.
- Board pins on the left include: A5/SCL, A4/SDA, AREF, GND, D13/SCK, D12/MISO, D11 PWM/MOSI, D10 PWM/SS, D9 PWM, D8, D7, D6 PWM, D5 PWM, D4, D3 PWM, D2, D1/TX, and D0/RX.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: LED Bar Graph module.
Purpose: Demonstrates a 10-segment LED bar graph, labeled "KYX-B10R" on the side. 
Technical details: The component consists of 10 rectangular LED segments arranged vertically. In the provided illustration, the bottom-most segment is illuminated in red, while the remaining nine segments are unlit (gray). 
Uncertainty: None.

Component: LED Bar Graph module.
Purpose: Demonstrates the physical appearance of a 10-segment LED bar graph used in Project 3.1.
Technical details: The component features ten rectangular segments arranged vertically. The text "KYX-B10R" is printed on the left side of the dark casing. The bottom-most segment is illuminated red, while the remaining nine segments are unlit (white/grey).
Uncertainty: None.

Component: PWM signal waveform diagrams.
Purpose: Demonstrates the relationship between Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) duty cycles (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and their corresponding analog signal voltage outputs.
Technical details: Five vertically stacked charts plot Voltage (U) against time (t). Each chart features a blue square wave (DIGITAL) representing the signal and a horizontal green line (ANALOG) representing the effective voltage. Y-axes range from 0 to 5V. In the 50% duty cycle chart, arrows label the "Period" (full cycle duration) and "Pulse width" (duration of high level). The analog voltage level increases proportionally with the duty cycle, moving from 0V at 0% duty cycle to 5V at 100% duty cycle.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Hardware connection diagram for a control board and breadboard.
Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit configuration to control four LEDs at different brightness levels using PWM-capable pins.
Technical details: The Freenove control board is connected to a breadboard. Four LEDs are placed on the breadboard, each with an associated resistor. Connections are as follows:
- Pin GND to the breadboard negative rail (black wire).
- Pin 10 (PWM) to the first LED/resistor path (yellow wire).
- Pin 9 (PWM) to the second LED/resistor path (green wire).
- Pin 6 (PWM) to the third LED/resistor path (gray wire).
- Pin 5 (PWM) to the fourth LED/resistor path (white wire).
The breadboard features rows labeled A-J and columns 1-30. LEDs are positioned across rows F and E. Resistors bridge rows E and D.
Uncertainty: Wire colors and specific breadboard column coordinates are identified visually and may be subject to minor interpretation.

Component: Circuit schematic diagram.
Purpose: Demonstrates the hardware connection for driving four LEDs at different brightness levels using PWM-capable pins on a control board.
Technical details: The circuit consists of four parallel branches, each connecting a control board pin to an LED and a current-limiting resistor tied to ground.
- Pin 5 connects to the anode (pin 1) of LED1; the cathode (pin 2) connects to resistor R1 (220Ω), which leads to ground.
- Pin 6 connects to the anode of LED2; the cathode connects to R2 (220Ω), which leads to ground.
- Pin 9 connects to the anode of LED3; the cathode connects to R3 (220Ω), which leads to ground.
- Pin 10 connects to the anode of LED4; the cathode connects to R4 (220Ω), which leads to ground.
All resistors R1-R4 are labeled as 220Ω.

Component: Breadboard section with four through-hole LEDs.

Purpose: This image illustrates the physical layout of four red LEDs inserted into a breadboard.

Technical details: The image shows four red LEDs with their leads inserted into a standard solderless breadboard. The text visible in the upper portion shows partial labels "20" and "25", corresponding to the column markings on the breadboard. Each LED has two pins; the left pins are inserted into one row, and the right pins are inserted into an adjacent row below the central divider of the breadboard.

Uncertainty: The specific pin connections to a control board cannot be determined from this view, and the exact breadboard column numbers are partially obscured.

Component: Hardware connection diagram for Project 4.2 LED Blinking Smoothly.

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit wiring for an LED breathing light project using a Freenove Control Board and a breadboard.

Technical details:
- A red LED is inserted into breadboard coordinates column 26, rows F and G.
- A resistor connects the LED cathode (row E, column 26) to the breadboard's blue negative power rail. 
- A black jumper wire connects the blue negative power rail to the GND pin on the control board.
- An LED anode (row E, column 26) connects via a yellow jumper wire to digital PWM pin 5 on the control board.
- The control board features headers labeled SCL, SDA, AREF, GND, 13, 12, ~11, ~10, ~9, 8, 7, ~6, ~5, 4, ~3, 2, TX→1, RX←0 and analog inputs A0-A5.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Schematic diagram for Project 4.2 LED Blinking Smoothly.

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit configuration for controlling a single LED using PWM.

Technical details: The circuit connects "Pin 5" to the anode (pin 1) of "LED1". The cathode (pin 2) of "LED1" connects to pin 2 of resistor "R1". Resistor "R1" is labeled with a value of "220Ω" and has pin 1 connected to ground.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit schematic diagram.
Purpose: Demonstrates the recommended push button switch connection for digital input, where the control board pin detects 5V (high) when the switch is open and 0V (low) when closed.
Technical details: The circuit consists of a 5V supply connected to terminal 1 of resistor R1 (10kΩ). Terminal 2 of R1 connects to a junction shared with terminal 1 of switch S1 and terminal 1 of resistor R2 (10kΩ). Terminal 2 of R2 connects to the "Pin" input. Terminal 2 of switch S1 connects to ground. Switch S1 is represented as a normally open push button.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit diagram for a push button switch input.

Purpose: Demonstrates a digital input circuit configuration where the detected level is opposite to the standard pull-up configuration (input is LOW when button is unpressed and HIGH when pressed).

Technical details:
- Power: 5V rail connected to pin 1 of resistor R1 (10kΩ).
- Switch (S1): Pin 1 connects to pin 2 of R1. Pin 2 of S1 connects to ground and pin 1 of resistor R4 (10kΩ).
- Output: Pin 2 of resistor R4 connects to the input "Pin".
- Ground: Connected to the junction of S1 pin 2 and R4 pin 1.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Hardware Connection diagram for Project 5.1, showing a breadboard interfaced with a Freenove Control Board.

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit wiring to detect a push button state using the control board and trigger an LED.

Technical details:
- Control board pins used: 5V (red wire to breadboard power rail), GND (black wire to breadboard), pin 12 (yellow wire to button circuit), pin 9 (green wire to LED anode).
- Breadboard: Includes one push button switch, one LED, and two resistors.
- Wiring: A 10kΩ resistor connects the button node to GND (black wire path); another 10kΩ resistor connects the button node to 5V; a 220Ω resistor is in series with the LED anode.
- Connections: The yellow wire from pin 12 monitors the button's input signal. The green wire from pin 9 controls the LED.

Uncertainty: Resistor color bands are partially obscured, making the exact resistance values uncertain from the visual alone (values provided per project documentation).

Component: Schematic diagram for Project 5.1, "Control LED with Push Button Switch."

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit configuration for using a push button as an input signal to control an LED output via a control board.

Technical details:
- Push button section: A 5V supply connects through a 10kΩ resistor (R1) to a junction. This junction connects to a switch (S1) which leads to ground, and to pin 12 via a 10kΩ resistor (R2).
- LED section: Pin 9 connects to the anode of LED1 (Red, 633nm). The cathode of LED1 connects to ground through a 220Ω resistor (R3).
- Pin assignments: Pin 12 is designated for button status detection; Pin 9 is designated for LED drive.
- Component labels: Resistors R1 (10kΩ), R2 (10kΩ), R3 (220Ω), Switch S1, and LED1.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Hardware connection diagram for a control board and breadboard.

Purpose: Demonstrates the circuit wiring for Project 5.1, connecting a push button switch and an LED to a control board.

Technical details:
- Control board pins 9, 12, GND, and 5V are utilized.
- A red jumper wire connects the control board 5V pin (labeled 5V) to the breadboard power rail.
- A black jumper wire connects the control board GND pin to the breadboard common rail.
- A yellow jumper wire connects control board pin 12 to the push button switch row on the breadboard.
- A green jumper wire connects control board pin 9 to the LED row on the breadboard.
- Components on the breadboard include one LED, one push button switch, and three resistors (R1, R2, R3).
- Resistors are connected between the power/ground rails and the switch/LED terminals to form the pull-up/pull-down and current-limiting configurations described in the project.

Uncertainty: Resistor values cannot be visually confirmed from the color bands.

Component: Circuit Knowledge diagram, Project 5.2.
Purpose: Demonstrates the concept of "switch bounce" by comparing an ideal state signal to a virtual (bouncing) state signal during push button press and release cycles.
Technical details: The top plot (green line) shows the "Ideal state," with a clean transition between high and low voltage levels. The bottom plot (blue line) shows the "virtual state" with mechanical vibrations (buffeting) during press and release transitions. Vertical red dashed lines align the transition phases across both plots. Both charts map voltage (U) on the vertical axis against time (t) on the horizontal axis. Annotations above the plots label the timeline segments as "press", "stable", "release", and "stable".
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Circuit Knowledge diagram, Parallel communication section.

Purpose: Illustrates the concept of parallel communication where multiple bits are transmitted simultaneously across multiple lines.

Technical details: The image shows a schematic representing multiple parallel data lines between two horizontal borders. It displays four distinct vertical columns, each containing a stack of seven rectangular blocks representing data bits, followed by an ellipsis indicating additional parallel lines.

Uncertainty: None.

Component: Communication diagram.
Purpose: Illustrates the concept of parallel communication where multiple data bits are transmitted simultaneously.
Technical details: The image shows four parallel columns of rectangles representing bits being fed into a narrowing funnel-like structure, transitioning into a single line of bits exiting to the right. This visual represents the transition from parallel data flow to serial data flow.
Uncertainty: None.

Component: Arduino IDE software interface (version 1.6.8).
